subject: Renewal addendum: Dedicated GPU pool + warm-pool & scale-up SLA
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-13T10:02:00Z
Subject: Renewal addendum: Dedicated GPU pool + warm-pool & scale-up SLA

Kevin/Linda —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Based on the usage patterns you shared (peak windows on weekdays, bursty batch jobs overnight), we drafted an addendum that updates your Dedicated contract for the next 12 months. High level:

- Add 20x A100-equivalent GPUs into a reserved pool (min-reserved capacity for guaranteed throughput).
- Warm-pool: maintain N=4 warm replicas per instance type to reduce cold-starts for interactive workloads.
- Autoscale policy: set minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=60 (per-region), scale-up aggressive buckets with target scale-up lag <=30s for small bursts and <=90s for large saturations.
- Throughput guarantee: target 1.2M tokens/min sustained across the reserved pool during defined business hours (Mon-Fri 8am-8pm PT) with penalties / credits if not met (see SLA section).

Attached: proposed addendum PDF and a short cost impact table. Key open items for you:
1) Confirm warm-pool sizing (we recommended 4 warm replicas based on your 95th-percentile request size).
2) Approve the min/max replica bands and the target scale-up lag (30s for top priority lanes).
3) Confirm billing contact and preferred signature flow (DocuSign vs signed PDF).

If this looks good, we'll route the addendum to your procurement contact and schedule a short runbook review with your ops team so they can see the warm-pool behavior in the Dedicated Console before go-live.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270415_acme-dedicated-addendum.pdf (PDF, 4 pages), cost_impact_table.xlsx (Excel)

Karthik —

Thanks, appreciate the clear summary. A couple of quick questions from our side:

- Warm-pool cost: Does the run rate for warm replicas get billed at the same rate as active replicas, or is there a reduced rate since they are preloaded but idle? We need to model steady-state monthly cost.
- Cold-start mitigation: if a warm replica is evicted (e.g., node failure) what is the expected time to restore KV cache and be fully warmed?
- MinReplicas enforcement: we run an overnight ETL that needs capacity spikes. If minReplicas=2, will that block scale-up during heavy batch runs?

If possible please call out a scenario in the addendum showing cost delta for 0/2/4 warm replicas and a 3-month projection. Otherwise looks directionally fine.

Kevin

VP, ML Platforms
Acme Analytics

Kevin —

Quick answers (and note for procurement folks):

- Warm-pool billing: warm replicas are billed at ~65% of an active replica in the proposed pricing model. They are compute-ready but not counted against active inference throughput pricing; we model them as reserved infrastructure (see cost_impact_table.xlsx). I'll attach an exported table to the hub link.
- Cold-start recovery: if a warm replica is lost due to node failure, we can rehydrate on a replacement node using cached KV prefetch. Typical rewarm time for a single large model (20B) is ~35–45s; for smaller family models expect <20s. This assumes we can schedule replacement capacity within the reserved pool.
- MinReplicas behavior: minReplicas is a floor for active instances. Autoscaler will still scale up beyond the floor for bursts. The concern is scale-up lag — with the warm-pool we can route high-priority lanes to warm replicas immediately; batch jobs will scale out under the normal autoscaler window. If you want batch jobs to bypass warm-pool eviction logic, we can mark certain queues as "batch-priority" so they get dedicated warm replicas at lower cost.

Recommended conservative defaults for your profile: minReplicas=2, warmReplicasPerType=4, maxReplicas=60, targetScaleUpLag=30s for interactive lanes, 90s for low-priority batch. We can adjust the SLA window if you prefer extended business hours.

Runbook & ops notes: pending runbook review (internal link below) — we recommend a pre-rollout simulation with 2x peak synthetic traffic to validate cache-hit rates and recovery.

Runbook: internal://runbooks/dedicated-warmpool-deploy
Cost export: https://files.redwood.ai/exports/ACME-cost-20270414.csv

— Sergio

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
